title: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
analysis: Keep unhinted shift simplification. Easy gives away both identity and exact values; moderate includes full-turn and near-duplicate variants. Non-axis hard is substantially source-aligned.

title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
analysis: Easy/moderate decomposition hints match the imports. Hard reverses an expanded identity, removes the decomposition, then expands again; no imported hard anchor supports that synthesis task.

title: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
analysis: Easy axis shifts and moderate non-axis shifts match imports. Hard invents weighted pairs of cosine expansions; some phase-equivalent pairs collapse to one ordinary shift. Also avoid negative entries after a printed minus.

title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products
analysis: Direct easy practice is useful. Moderate sometimes names the resulting sine/doubled angle in the prompt. Quartic hard requires factoring/Pythagorean recognition: plausible transfer, but no hard imported anchor establishes its calibration.

title: Using the Double-Angle Formula Multiple Times
analysis: Easy states the identity and both substitutions in sequence, giving away the skill. Moderate drops the reciprocal-cancellation family (five of six moderate imports) even though a constructor branch exists. Reciprocal hard families are source-supported.

title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Ratios
analysis: Strongest alignment: students must independently select the doubled-angle rewrite, cancel/rewrite ratios, and use source-supported factoring in hard. Difficulty overlap between a source easy cotangent quotient and generated moderate deserves calibration, not a blanket reduction.

title: Finding Exact Value of a Trigonometric Expression Using the Double-Angle Formula
analysis: Generated product/square/reciprocal families match the source progression; guidance stays in the solution. One partial imported question ends its worked solution with the wrong sign in the original expression.

title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions
analysis: Easy direct and moderate common-factor recognition are aligned. Quartic hard adds difference-of-squares/Pythagorean work without imported hard anchors. Bank-first angle ladders create clustered variants. Two imported radio banks have valid alternatives marked wrong.

title: Using Alternative Forms of Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Expressions
analysis: Easy/moderate alternatives and common-factor recognition match imports. Hard invents quartic regrouping and a second double-angle application, anchored to a generated prototype. A source bank is ambiguous and another needs a response-form caveat.

title: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula
analysis: The expanded-perfect-square hard family is genuinely imported. However, the only stored generated hard question uses a known 135-degree angle and evaluates directly to zero, bypassing the target identity; exclude or deliberately limit these cases. Source operator notation also needs repair.

title: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
analysis: Easy/moderate are largely aligned. Hard invents sums/differences of two shifted sines and mixed-radical coefficient collection without imported hard anchors. One moderate frame adds unnecessary double negation.

title: Finding Exact Values Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
analysis: Good distinction: supplied decomposition in easy/moderate, independent decomposition in hard is directly supported by imported hard q-119007. Preserve one forward identity application; do not add the cosine hard wrapper.

title: Simplifying Expressions in Radians Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
analysis: Easy supplies the identity and both exact values although no easy import does so. Moderate axis and hard non-axis tasks are mostly appropriate. Renaming-only repeats and one imported solution angle typo need attention.
